Dietary polyphenols in modulating glycolipid metabolism to suppress HCC

Mechanisms of dietary polyphenols in modulating glycolipid metabolism to suppress HCC. This schematic illustrates the coordinated mechanisms through which dietary polyphenols concurrently regulate the interconnected glucose and lipid metabolic pathways to suppress hepatocellular carcinoma. Polyphenols ameliorate glucose metabolism by enhancing insulin sensitivity through the IRS/PI3K/AKT signaling axis and inhibiting gluconeogenesis via downregulation of G6Pase and PEPCK. Concurrently, they reshape lipid homeostasis by activating AMPK/SIRT1 to suppress SREBP-1c-mediated lipogenesis and key enzymes including ACC and FASN, while promoting fatty acid β-oxidation through the PPARα/CPT-1 pathway. Additional modulation of cholesterol metabolism occurs through FXR activation and LDLR upregulation. Collectively, these multi-targeted actions restore metabolic balance, further supported by the activation of the Nrf2-mediated antioxidant response and suppression of NF-κB/NLRP3-driven inflammation, ultimately inhibiting HCC progression
